OwnerFields:
      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      type: object
      properties:
        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: The postal address of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: The telephone number of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          pattern: '^[0-9]*$'
          example: '6085551023'
      required:
        - firstName
        - lastName
        - address
        - city
        - telephone
    Owner:
      title: Owner
      description: A pet owner.
      allOf:
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/OwnerFields'
        - type: object

## Summary

I implemented required-field validation for `POST /api/owners` following the project's OfficeFloor function-injection conventions.

**The problem:** The existing pipeline relied on the generated DTO's bean-validation annotations (`@Valid`), which produce a `MethodArgumentNotValidException` rendered as a `schemaValidationErrors` body — not the `errors` array of field names the spec requires. Bean validation also wouldn't reliably treat a whitespace-only value (e.g. `"   "`) as blank.

**Changes:**

1. **`ValidateOwnerFields`** (new function) — first step of the pipeline. Binds `@RequestBody`, checks each of `firstName`, `lastName`, `address`, `city`, `telephone` for null-or-blank (`String.isBlank()` catches whitespace-only), collects *every* offending field, and throws a checked `OwnerFieldsRequiredException(errors)`. On success it republishes the body via `Out<OwnerFieldsDto>`.

2. **`OwnerFieldsRequiredException`** (new checked exception) — carries the list of offending field names.

3. **`OwnerFieldsRequiredExceptionHandler`** + escalation YAML — responds `400` with body `{"errors": [...]}`.

4. **`BuildOwner`** — changed from binding `@Valid @RequestBody` to consuming the already-published `@Val OwnerFieldsDto`, since the body may only be bound once per pipeline.

5. **`owners.POST.yml`** — added the `validate` step ahead of `build`.

**Result:** missing/blank required fields → `400` with `errors` listing each field name; a complete owner still succeeds (`2xx`). All 3 acceptance tests pass and the build is green.
